items.stem: Which requirement statement is best written?

options.text: The system shall email the customer within 2 minutes of claim approval
options.rationale: Correct: it is specific, measurable and testable.

options.text: The system shall use a dropdown menu on the approval screen
options.rationale: This specifies design, not a requirement of business need.
'User-friendly' is subjective and not verifiable as written.

items.explanation: Correct: it is specific, measurable and testable.

items.stem: Which statements about non-functional requirements are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: They describe qualities such as performance, security or availability
options.rationale: Correct: non-functional requirements constrain how well the system behaves.

options.text: They should still be specified in testable terms
options.rationale: Correct: a target like '99.9% uptime' makes them verifiable.

options.text: They define the specific features the system provides

options.rationale: Well-written non-functional requirements include measurable targets.

items.explanation: Correct: non-functional requirements constrain how well the system behaves.

items.stem: An analyst presents a 'current' process map that actually shows how work should ideally flow. Why is this a problem?

options.text: Improvement decisions will be based on a process that does not reflect reality
options.rationale: Correct: an inaccurate as-is hides the real bottlenecks and risks wrong fixes.

options.text: Ideal processes can never be drawn
options.rationale: To-be maps are valid; the error is mislabelling it as as-is.

options.text: Swimlanes are not allowed in as-is maps

options.rationale: Handoffs are exactly what an as-is map should expose.

items.explanation: Correct: an inaccurate as-is hides the real bottlenecks and risks wrong fixes.
